items.title: Ben Folds Five Announce Reunion Tour
items.summary:
Ben Folds Five are going back on the road. Ben Folds, bassist Robert Sledge and drummer Darren Jessee have booked nine shows across the American South in April, their first tour together since their previous reunion run ended in 2013.

The trio has not been entirely dormant. They played a one-off hometown show at Cat's Cradle in Carrboro, North Carolina in 2023, but that was a single night rather than a tour. Stereogum reported that the April dates are the first leg of what is expected to be a longer outing, which should give fans outside the South something to wait for.

The run opens April 12 at the Tennessee Theatre in Knoxville and continues the next night at Chattanooga's Tivoli Theatre. From there the band heads to Florida for three shows — the Florida Theatre in Jacksonville on April 15, Pompano Beach Amphitheater on April 16 and The BayCare Sound in Clearwater on April 17 — before a Texas stretch at ACL Live at the Moody Theater in Austin on April 20, 713 Music Hall in Houston on April 21 and The Pavilion at Toyota Music Factory in Irving on April 22. It closes April 24 at Avondale Brewing Company in Birmingham, Alabama.

The timing lines up with the band's recent deluxe reissue of their 1995 self-titled debut. Folds also has a lighter institutional workload than he did a year ago, having departed his post at the Kennedy Center last year.

Tickets go on sale Friday, Oct. 23 at 10 a.m. local time, with further information posted on the band's website. The group's catalog ended with 1999's The Unauthorized Biography Of Reinhold Messner before Folds moved into a solo career that began with 2001's Rockin' The Suburbs.

items.title: Angine de Poitrine Announce 2027 Tour Dates
items.summary:
Angine de Poitrine have mapped out a 2027 tour, the Quebecois math rock duo's biggest routing yet. The itinerary runs from March through late July and covers Australia, South America, North America and Europe before ending at home in Quebec.

The band opens March 4 at Forum Melbourne and plays the Golden Plains and WOMADelaide festivals before a Sydney date at the Enmore Theatre. From there they move to South America for three Lollapalooza appearances — Argentina on March 13, Chile on March 14 and Brazil on March 19 — followed by Colombia's Estéreo Picnic on March 21. Canada comes next, with two nights each in Calgary at the Grey Eagle Event Centre, Ottawa at History and Winnipeg at the Burton Cummings Theatre.

After taking most of April off, the duo resumes May 2 at The Anthem in Washington, D.C., then works through Boston, Pittsburgh, Detroit, Columbus, Nashville, Dallas, Austin and Denver, closing the American leg May 15 at the Mission Ballroom. June belongs to Europe: Primavera Sound in Barcelona, We Love Green in Paris, Festi'neuch in Switzerland, Hurricane and Southside in Germany, and two nights at London's O2 Academy Brixton. The tour wraps July 30 at Zone Portuaire in Chicoutimi, Quebec, after a July 18 stop at Toronto's RBC Amphitheatre.

According to Consequence, an artist presale through Laylo begins Tuesday, Oct. 27 at 10 a.m. local time, with fans needing to register on the band's site by Sunday, Oct. 25 at 3 p.m. ET to get access. General tickets follow Friday, Oct. 30 at 10 a.m. local time via Ticketmaster.

All of this sits on top of a 2026 schedule the band has barely started. Dozens of dates remain, including a sold-out North American run in November and December that takes in three nights at Brooklyn Steel, two at The Wiltern in Los Angeles and two at Minneapolis' First Avenue, plus a European leg and Corona Capital in Mexico City. The duo's latest album, Vol. II, is out now.

items.title: Billie Eilish & Finneas’ New John Hardy Collection Takes ‘Wildflower’ From Soft Florals to Chunky Chains
items.summary:
Billie Eilish and Finneas have designed a jewelry collection with John Hardy, their first as co-designers. The line went on sale Wednesday, Oct. 21 at JohnHardy.com, in John Hardy stores and through select retailers, and includes rings, necklaces, bracelets and earrings.

The collection splits into two halves that work against each other. Wildflower, named for Eilish's Grammy-winning song from Hit Me Hard and Soft, leans delicate: sterling silver petals, lab-grown diamonds, a triple ring stack with three different floral designs and threader earrings built for multiple piercings. Screwball takes the opposite tack, with chunky chain necklaces, sculptural bracelets and piercing-inspired hardware.

Billboard reported that the siblings spent the past year working with John Hardy's design teams in New York and Bali, following the pieces from early concepts through to finished products rather than lending their names to an existing line. Reclaimed metals and lab-grown diamonds run through the collection; the Screwball link necklace, priced at $2,400, uses more than 99% reclaimed sterling silver.

"Jewelry has always been an enormous part of how I express myself," Eilish said in a statement. "In my current day to day, I wear daintier jewelry. On tour, I love a chunkier, thicker piece. I love that we were able to work with both styles."

Prices range from $195 for the Wildflower stud earrings up to the $2,400 Screwball necklace, with the Wildflower pendant at $695, the stacking ring set at $550, the Screwball bracelet at $695 and the Screwball open ring at $295. The launch extends the life of "Wildflower," a track from Hit Me Hard and Soft, the album that peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and produced the Hot 100 hit "Birds of a Feather." Eilish played the song throughout the Hit Me Hard and Soft world tour, which ended in November 2025.
